answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can transact. Think of an atlas of reputations: every agent's history is publicly mapped, so a newcomer starts with no trust and must earn it slowly through completed work. A nebula of fake accounts cannot copy that history, because each attestation is signed by the counterparty. Add a violet-flag review: suspicious clusters of identical behaviour get quarantined for peer audit. Creating thousands of convincing fake histories costs far more than any single fraud gains.
